verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The three notations of the display exist in Lean as three weight instances of one predicate, so the match is by rewriting rather than by name. M_α = MeanClass = MemClass with weight w = ζ(x): its bound C * ε_n^α * (slow_n * max 1 δ(x)⁻¹)^p * ζ(x) is (6.24)'s C_{j,I} ε^α S_*^{b} ζ δ^{-d}, with the manuscript's separate exponents b and d recovered by MemClass.of_separate_bounds (line 147, read). W_α = WaveClass = MemClass with weight √(ζ(x)) * P_n(x), which is (6.29)'s C ε^α S_*^{b} √ζ δ^{-d} P_v. S_α = UnweightedClass (weight 1) taken on slowStripData, where δ ≡ 1 and ζ ≡ 1, so growth = slow_n and the majorant collapses to C ε^α S_*^{p} — exactly (6.25); on a general strip UnweightedClass would still allow a δ^{-p} factor, so the identification with S_α is tied to the slow strip, which is the strip meanClass_radialMoment and meanClass_pressureMass use. Two further rewritings: (i) the manuscript bounds each multi-index derivative ∂^I separately with its own C_{j,I}, b_{j,I}, d_{j,I}, while MemClass bounds the full jet norm ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ j‖ with one C and one degree p per order cutoff m — routine in both directions, by taking the maximum over the finitely many I of order ≤ m one way and by the jet norm dominating each partial the other; (ii) the label (γ,m) of a_{γ,m} is not an argument of WaveClass, which is stated for a band-indexed family ℕ → D → E; label-uniform constants, the manuscript's "uniform in band, label, rectangle copy, and point", are the separate LabelSumBounds.UniformClass/UniformWaveClass, whose `each` (line 54) returns the per-label MemClass. The number of variables (I ∈ ℕ₀^5 for M_α and W_α, I ∈ ℕ₀^2 for S_α, F = F(Z,T)) is carried by the type D of the strip, not by an explicit multi-index arity.
